turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I did her observations just now. Blood pressure is 128 over 82, and her pulse is 88. You can go in, doctor's waiting.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, sister. Have a seat, both of you. There's a note about a screening camp, but tell me in your own words what's brought you.

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok, so, from my side. I'm pregnant, twenty-two weeks, and I came because I need my own blood checked. I don't want to sit at home guessing about the baby, I want the test done on me.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The camp was me, ja. Community hall in Phoenix, last month. They said I've got thalassaemia trait, the beta one, and then she—

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): And then I just couldn't sleep properly. I'm up at two, sometimes three, going over and over it, what if the baby gets the serious kind, what if we left it too late, and I know googling at night is stupid but I still do it.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. Pause there. Any spotting or bleeding?
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also needs to tell you about the tablets, the clinic never—
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No bleeding, not even a spot, I look every morning, which is probably too much. But the tablets, let me give you the whole list so we don't leave one out.

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Every morning I take amlodopine, five milligrams, for the pressure. The sugar tablets are metforman, 500 milligrams with breakfast and again at supper, for the sugar. The cholesterol one at night for the cholesterol, twenty milligrams, and I cannot remember the proper name of that one. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, one teaspoon in warm water, I drink it.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mmm. I'm minded to keep this simple. Just a full blood count today, see you back in a month, and we park the electrophoresis for now.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Except the letter is not a maybe. It says beta thalassaemia trait, confirmed. And her mother's family is from Gujarat. The camp sister said that actually matters.

[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, Mom is Gujarati, my dad is coloured, from the Cape, and I've been so anxious I get a tight feeling in my chest whenever I start thinking about it. Not a pain, just tight, and the whole thing is exhausting, honestly, round and round.

[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Confirmed beta trait, and Gujarati ancestry. Then no, scratch the simple plan, I shouldn't have parked it. We'll do the full blood count and the haemoglobin electrophoresis, both, I'm booking them today, and I'm referring the two of you for genetic counselling.

[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say where I've landed. The severe disease needs the trait from both of you. If it's only your husband, the baby can still be a carrier, but not that severe illness. Working impression, nothing confirmed: we don't know if you carry it, so the risk stays unassigned until the electrophoresis is back.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the electrophoresis shows you're a carrier as well, then we'd add DNA studies. If it's clear, we don't. I'm not ordering DNA this morning.

[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Right, that helps. And the tablets, must I carry on with every one of them, the amlodopine and the metforman and the cholesterol one and the powder? I didn't want to chop and change and then cause some other problem with the pressure or the sugar.

[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the amlodipine, five milligrams in the morning, and the metformin, 500 twice a day. Stop the cholesterol one, skip tonight, we don't use those in pregnancy. Leave the Ayurvedic powder as well, I have no idea what's in it.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So when do we come back? My roster is hectic and I need to—
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two weeks. Not the month I said earlier, ignore that. We'll look at the results together. Get reception to book it.
[SEG0020] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put the bloods down for Thursday morning. Forms will be ready at the desk. You don't need to fast.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Thursday works, I bookkeep from home so I can move people around. Umm, the sleeping, it's every night since, uh...
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when, roughly? And apart from that tight feeling, any trouble with your breathing or your chest?
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three weeks. Camp was on the 12th, I'm pretty sure she—

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No, it wasn't three weeks. Err, I can't pin the date at all, sometime after we got the letter, I really don't know. Breathing is fine, no shortness of breath. The tightness only comes when the worry kicks in.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your own family, your mom, dad, siblings, cousins. Any thalassaemia, or a child needing regular transfusions?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I phoned my mother and we went through the whole lot, even the cousins in India, and there's nothing like that, she would have remembered if there was.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Keep the pressure tablet and the sugar tablets exactly as they are. No cholesterol tablet, no powder. If you bleed, or the belly pain is severe, or you feel faint, don't sit on it for two weeks, go to maternity assessment the same day.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The genetic counselling, that's actually booked, hey? Not a we'll-see?
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's booked from my side. I'll send the referral to the hospital genetics clinic today, and they'll give you the date. Not a maybe.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Shame, thank you. I'll try to stop reading things at two in the morning, it just makes my head worse, I know that, I just... ja. See you Thursday.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): Come past the desk, I'll print the lab slip and write in the two-week visit. Sharp.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
